findings.title: Cleanup logs every successful batch at Error level, including full ID lists
findings.body: The new batch callbacks log at Error level during normal, successful operation: lines 534, 537, 554, 557 (CleanAnnotations) and 576, 579 (CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags) all call r.log.Error(...). These fire on every cleanup cycle and every batch, and they dump the complete slice of fetched IDs into the log line (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries, potentially tens of thousands of IDs per line). This produces massive log lines and constant false error-level noise that can trip alerting on error logs and bury real errors. The 'err', err key/value pairs log a value that is always nil at those points, indicating these are leftover debug statements. They should be Debug level (or removed) and should not serialize the entire ID slice.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute for all cleanup jobs, undocumented
findings.body: The PR is about splitting the annotation cleanup queries, but it also changes the CleanUpService ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This makes every cleanup job run 10x more often, not just annotation cleanup: filesystem scans of the images and CSV directories (cleanUpTmpFiles), expired snapshot/dashboard-version/image deletion, user invite expiry, short URL and query history cleanup. Each minute now scans directories and issues DELETEs against many tables, and since each run has a 9-minute timeout, a slow run means cleanup work executes essentially back-to-back with no idle gap. This behavior change is not mentioned in the PR description and affects operators' DB and I/O load; if the motivation is to compensate for the new split queries under-deleting annotations, only the annotation job cadence should change.

findings.title: SQLite inline-ID path builds the IN list with quadratic fmt.Sprintf concatenation
findings.body: In deleteByIDs, the SQLite fallback builds the ID list via values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside the loop, which copies the entire accumulated string on every iteration — O(n²) byte copying. With the large batch sizes this path exists for (the new test uses a batch size of 32767), that is on the order of gigabytes of transient copying per batch on every cleanup cycle. A strings.Builder plus strconv.AppendInt would make it linear. Related minor points: the comment 'SQLite has a parameter limit of 999' is outdated for SQLite >= 3.32.0 (which supports 32766 variables, as the new test's name acknowledges), and the branch is keyed off the configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize rather than len(ids), so even a final 5-row batch takes the string-building path when the configured batch size exceeds 999.
